parking_rules.summary: Many NYC streets have alternate side parking (ASP) for street cleaning; days and hours are on the signs for each block. You cannot park on the side being cleaned for the whole posted time, even after the sweeper has passed.
parking_rules.quote: You cannot park on the side of the street that is being cleaned when ASP rules are in effect. The rules apply for the length of the entire block, and for the entire time posted on the sign, even if the street sweeper has already passed.

parking_rules.summary: ASP is not in effect on Sundays, and is suspended on listed legal and religious holidays, in severe weather and in emergencies.
parking_rules.quote: ASP rules are suspended on certain legal and religious holidays each year, during severe weather, and for emergencies. On Sundays, ASP is not in effect

parking_rules.summary: The city may suspend ASP for snow or emergencies, sometimes announced late in the day; ASP is restored after a snowfall so plows can clear the curb lane. No citywide snow-route parking ban was found on the pages read.
parking_rules.quote: NYC may suspend ASP regulations because of inclement weather or emergencies. The decision is sometimes made late in the day since weather patterns can change fast. NYC restores ASP regulations after a snowfall.

parking_rules.summary: No citywide overnight street-parking ban appears on NYC DOT's parking pages; what applies is whatever the signs on the block say, and the most restrictive sign wins.
parking_rules.quote: If there is more than one sign posted for the same area, the more restrictive one is the one in effect. If a sign is missing on a block, the remaining posted regulations are the ones that are in effect. Please check the entire block and read all signs carefully before you park.

parking_rules.summary: All of NYC is a tow-away zone: a car parked illegally, or with a missing or expired registration or inspection sticker, may be towed.
parking_rules.quote: All of New York City is a designated Tow Away Zone under the State's Vehicle and Traffic Law. This means that any vehicle parked or operated illegally, or with missing or expired registration or inspection stickers, may be towed.

parking_rules.summary: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is illegal.
parking_rules.quote: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of either side of a fire hydrant

parking_rules.summary: Meters are not in effect on Sundays or on the six major legal holidays. Other hours are on the meter or sign.
parking_rules.quote: Metered regulations are not in effect on Sundays nor major legal holidays (New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day).

parking_rules.summary: Passenger meter rates outside Manhattan's core: $2.50 first hour and $5.00 second hour in business districts such as Downtown Flushing and Jamaica; $2.00 / $3.00 in neighborhood retail districts; $1.50 / $2.50 elsewhere.
parking_rules.quote: Zone 1 - Business Districts outside of Manhattan (e.g., Downtown Brooklyn, Downtown Flushing, and Jamaica; Manhattan 125th Street) $2.50 $5.00 Zone 2 - Neighborhood Retail Districts $2.00 $3.00 Zone 3 - All Other Metered Locations $1.50 $2.50

parking_rules.summary: NYC DOT garages sell monthly permits: Court Square (Queens) $400, Borough Hall (Brooklyn) $330, Bay Ridge $275, Jerome-190th Street (Bronx) $250, Delancey and Essex (Manhattan) $600. No monthly rate is listed for the Queens Family Court garage in Jamaica.
Monthly garage permits are reserved online, first come first served, from five days before the month starts; a New York State driver's license check is run at reservation.
parking_rules.quote: Reservations open on the website five days before the first of the month at 10 am. All reservations are made for the upcoming month, on a first-come, first-served basis. A New York State Department of Motor Vehicles driver's license check is performed at the time of the reservation.

parking_rules.summary: Municipal parking fields (open lots) do not allow overnight parking; they close at the posted hour, typically 10 PM.
parking_rules.quote: Municipal parking fields do not allow overnight parking. The fields close as shown in the posted regulations for each facility. Parking after posted hours may result in a summons and leaves the vehicle at risk as there is no security at the closed facilities.

parking_rules.summary: Quarterly permits at municipal parking fields: Flushing #4 $300, Steinway #1 (Astoria) $500, Bayside $500, Brighton Beach $625, Sheepshead Bay #1 $300, Canarsie $300, Bronxdale $400.
parking_rules.quote: Bronxdale Municipal Parking Field $400 Bensonhurst #1 Municipal Parking Field $300 Brighton Beach Municipal Parking Field $625 Canarsie Municipal Parking Field $300 Sheepshead Bay #1 Municipal Parking Field $300 Bayside Municipal Parking Field $500 Flushing #4 Municipal Parking Field $300 Steinway #1 Municipal Parking Field $500

dog_rules.summary: Every dog in NYC must be licensed and wear the tag in public. A license costs $8.50 a year for a spayed or neutered dog; $34 for an unaltered dog over 4 months.
dog_rules.quote: All dogs in New York City must have licenses, and the licenses must be attached to their collars while in public.

dog_rules.summary: License fee: $8.50 a year if spayed or neutered; if not, $8.50 under 4 months old and $34 over 4 months.
dog_rules.quote: Licenses for spayed or neutered dogs of any age cost $8.50 per year. If your dog is not spayed or neutered, a license will cost $8.50 if the dog is under 4 months old, or $34 if it is older than 4 months.

dog_rules.summary: In any public place a dog must be on a leash no longer than six feet.
dog_rules.quote: a person who owns, possesses or controls a dog shall not permit it to be in any public place or in any open or unfenced area abutting on a public place unless the dog is effectively restrained by a leash or other restraint not more than six feet long.

dog_rules.summary: In city parks dogs must be leashed except where Parks rules allow off-leash; the Health Code lets Parks allow off-leash in unenclosed areas only within a window that starts no earlier than 9 PM and ends by 9 AM. The Parks rules themselves could not be read (site bot-walled).
dog_rules.quote: Such rules shall include provisions that prohibit unrestrained dogs in unenclosed DOPR controlled areas and facilities except during a specified range of time, that shall not begin earlier than 9:00 P.M. and not extend past 9:00 A.M.

dog_rules.summary: With proof of a current license and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash in NYC Parks dog runs. The open-data list has 95 active runs (14 in Queens, 20 Brooklyn, 41 Manhattan, 15 Bronx, 5 Staten Island); see dog_parks.csv.
dog_rules.quote: With proof of current dog license and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash at New York City park dog runs

dog_rules.summary: Owners must pick up after their dog in all public areas; the fine is up to $250.
dog_rules.quote: If you do not clean up after your dog, you may be fined up to $250.
